title: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression pact
summary: Foreign ministers Joachim von Ribbentrop and Vyacheslav Molotov signed a ten-year non-aggression treaty in Moscow. A secret protocol divided Poland, the Baltic states, Finland and Romania into German and Soviet spheres of influence.
reason: Hitler wanted to attack Poland without facing a two-front war, and Stalin, distrusting Britain and France, sought time and territory.
significance: It cleared the way for the invasion of Poland a week later and the Soviet annexations that followed.
